articles.headline: Lock, Smith-Njigba have Seahawks 2-0 with Darnold ahead of schedule
articles.description: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said QB Sam Darnold could return to practice this week and did not rule out the possibility of him playing next Sunday. In the meantime, backup Drew Lock has Seattle 2-0, with plenty of help from receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
articles.body:
GLENDALE, Ariz. -- The Seattle Seahawks might get Sam Darnold back from his glute injury sooner than they initially expected. Coach Mike Macdonald said postgame Sunday that the quarterback's timetable has "shifted quite drastically" for the better.

Darnold could return to practice sometime this week, and after the Seahawks improved to 2-0 with a 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium, Macdonald didn't rule out Seattle's QB1 possibly playing next Sunday against the Washington Commanders (0-2).

Though Drew Lock's hot start to the season could give the Seahawks reason to take their time with Darnold, Macdonald insisted that the decision will be based on his readiness.

"If Sam can play, he's going to play," Macdonald said. "If Sam can't play, then Drew will play. It's pretty simple."

In the meantime, Lock is playing starter-level football, and he's getting plenty of help from Jaxon Smith-Njigba as well as last season's top-ranked scoring defense. Lock threw three more touchdown passes to the reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year on Sunday, and Macdonald's unit shut the door in the second half to turn a 7-7 score into a runaway victory.

In his first start since 2024, Lock completed 19 of 26 attempts for 235 yards and no interceptions. As he mostly did last week in helping rally the Seahawks to a season-opening win over the New England Patriots after Darnold went down on the game's fifth play, Lock kept the ball out of harm's way against Arizona, and he was sacked only once.

"Really proud of Drew, really happy for him," Macdonald said. "We're on the record in how we feel about him, so he just backed that up today. That's a 12 as one thing, everybody having each other's back. You just couldn't be happier for the guy. We just love him. All the things we said about him throughout the week, that was real. That was from the heart. Really proud of the way he played today. He did a tremendous job."

Lock's first touchdown pass to Smith-Njigba came on their second play from scrimmage, when the receiver used a head fake to get wide open behind Arizona's defense for an 82-yard score. They connected for a 7-yard touchdown in the third quarter and a 12-yarder in the fourth, both coming on third down.

Lock's lone touchdown pass in the opener was to Smith-Njigba.

"We've been having a special connection for a minute now, but I'm super happy [for] the way he just came in and carried himself and carried this team," Smith-Njigba said of Lock. "He shows time and time again how good he is."

Per ESPN Research, Smith-Njigba is the third player in franchise history with 150-plus receiving yards and three receiving TDs in a game, joining Tyler Lockett and Steve Largent (twice). Smith-Njigba now has an NFL-high 11 games with at least 100 receiving yards since the start of last season. He's the first Seahawk to catch three touchdown passes in a game since DK Metcalf in 2023.

articles.headline: Kirk Cousins' 'phenomenal' play has new-look Raiders at 2-0
articles.description: Kirk Cousins has done more than just help the Raiders transition through a rebuilding process after two games, leading Las Vegas to its first 2-0 record since 2021.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Kirk Cousins became the Las Vegas Raiders' starting quarterback to help jump-start the rebuild process under first-time head coach Klint Kubiak.

Cousins' presence has paid dividends thus far.

He threw for 253 yards, three touchdowns and an interception to lead the Raiders past the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 on Sunday afternoon at SoFi Stadium, improving to 2-0 for the first time since 2021.

Cousins had a 65.5% completion rate and posted a passer rating of 113.1. It was a performance that left wide receiver Tre Tucker clamoring about Cousins postgame, saying the 38-year-old signal-caller "can probably play until he is 60."

 

"It's still early, but the goal is to build something that way outlasts me," said Cousins, who has thrown six touchdown passes in two games. He is the second player in team history to record six touchdown passes in the first two games, joining former quarterback Ken Stabler in 1976.

Cousins proved that in Year 15, he still has a bit of arm strength. A week after he completed 1 of 7 pass attempts for 21 yards and two interceptions on throws for 10-plus air yards, he was effective on those throws. On attempts of 10-plus air yards, Cousins completed 8 of 12 passes for 181 yards, three touchdowns and an interception.

Cousins' interception with 9:05 to go in the first quarter was a result of Tucker slipping while running his route, which led to cornerback Cam Hart catching the ball. Cousins, however, had a nice response in the second quarter. With 12 minutes to go, Cousins completed a 40-yard touchdown pass to Tucker to give the Raiders a 7-0 lead.

During the final seconds of the quarter, Cousins found Tucker again for a 42-yard completion that set up a 59-yard field goal attempt from kicker Matt Gay to give Las Vegas a 10-7 lead at halftime. Tucker finished with five catches for 119 yards and a touchdown on seven targets.

"[Cousins] did a really good job of pushing the ball down the field," Kubiak said. "Our playmakers, like Tre, made some really big plays. It's something you're always trying to do every weekend."

Trailing by four points in the third quarter, Cousins helped the Raiders score 17 unanswered points to secure the victory. He engineered the comeback, starting with a 27-yard pass to wide receiver Dareke Young. Cousins tossed the ball to running back Ashton Jeanty, who threw it back to him before he found Young open down the field while a defender was closing in.

Three plays later, Cousins threw a 13-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Cody White. In the fourth quarter, both players connected for an 11-yard touchdown, which gave Las Vegas a 13-point advantage.

"He's elite, man. I'm so excited to play with him," Tucker said. "He does not look any bit old to me, and the things I see him doing in practice, he's doing in the games."

Kubiak said: "He's been phenomenal with the operations and leadership. I can't say enough great things about No. 8."

articles.headline: QB Baker Mayfield says Bucs need to 'fight our way out' of 0-2 start
articles.description: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield admitted to being "pretty shocked" the Bucs are 0-2 for the first time since he has been their quarterback and the first time since 2014 after losing to his former team, the Browns, 23-19.
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield admitted to being "pretty shocked" the Bucs are 0-2 for the first time since he has been their quarterback and the first time since 2014 after losing to his former team, the Cleveland Browns, 23-19.

"Pretty shocked. But it's where we're at. So we've got to fight our way out," said Mayfield, who could not lead the Bucs back from a 23-19 deficit against the team that selected him first overall in the 2018 NFL draft and traded him away in 2022.

Mayfield is now 0-2 against the Browns with his previous loss coming as a member of the Carolina Panthers, to whom the Browns traded him in 2022 after securing quarterback Deshaun Watson in a deal with the Houston Texans.

Mayfield told the "Fourth & South Podcast" earlier this summer that he had this game circled on the calendar since the schedule came out. When asked whether this loss stings more given the circumstances, he said, "No, [it] just stings more because we're 0-2."

"It's shooting ourselves in the foot, not making the plays when we need them, knowing that these are fixable things, but that also makes it more frustrating," Mayfield said. "But just got to get it corrected. We've got to be harder on ourselves, watch the tape, get those things fixed, flush it and move it on to the next."

The Browns grabbed the lead with 3:57 to go in regulation on a 17-yard touchdown pass from Watson to Blake Whiteheart that, with the PAT, made it 23-19. A lightning delay right at the two-minute mark sent the teams into the locker rooms for two hours and 12 minutes.

When play resumed, running back Bucky Irving converted a third-and-1 with a 6-yard run that brought the Bucs to the Cleveland 13-yard line. But a holding penalty on center Graham Barton on the very next play forced the Bucs into a second-and-14 situation from the Browns' 23.

On that play, Mayfield found rookie Ted Hurst III one-on-one on a go route against Mekhi Blackmon along the left sideline. Hurst, a third-round draft pick out of Georgia State who was brought in to help replace longtime X receiver Mike Evans and saw more targets than any other Bucs receiver Sunday, couldn't hang on to the ball as he slid into the end zone.

Hurst said rain wasn't a factor despite a heavy downpour that had visibly saturated the field and the ball. Still, those are conditions the Bucs have simulated in practice, including this week, in anticipation of inclement weather.

"No, honestly, I just have to make that play," Hurst said, adding that he thought he was going to score on the play.

After a 3-yard scramble from Mayfield, his last-gasp effort came on a fourth-and-11 throw to Emeka Egbuka, with whom Mayfield connected earlier on a 5-yard score. This time, however, Mayfield overthrew the second-year wideout.

articles.body:
Eight games made up Sunday's early window in Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season, and we have the best highlights, touchdowns and moments from all of them.

In a matchup of divisional rivalries, the Carolina Panthers dominated host and NFC South foe Atlanta Falcons, 34-3. And in a matchup of NFC North supremacy, the Minnesota Vikings held off the Chicago Bears, 9-3.

In the afternoon slate of games, the Denver Broncos defeated the Jacksonville Jaguars 20-13 and the Raiders took down AFC West rival Los Angeles Chargers.

articles.headline: 2026 MLB ABS challenge system tracker: Team, player rankings
articles.description: The ABS challenge system leaderboard ranks batters, catchers, teams and umpires throughout the MLB season.
articles.body:
Major League Baseball implemented the ABS challenge system for the 2026 season, which allows players to challenge a ball or strike call made by the plate umpire. Each team receives two challenges to start the game, and only batters, pitchers and catchers can challenge a call. If a team wins a challenge, it can keep challenging. If a team challenges incorrectly twice, it loses its challenges for the rest of the game.

articles.headline: Brewers set franchise record with 98th victory, beat Orioles 3-0 to complete sweep
articles.description: — William Contreras homered, and the Milwaukee Brewers earned their franchise-record 98th victory by beating the Baltimore Orioles 3-0 on Sunday night to complete a three-game sweep.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- — William Contreras homered, and the Milwaukee Brewers earned their franchise-record 98th victory by beating the Baltimore Orioles 3-0 on Sunday night to complete a three-game sweep.


              Cooper Pratt drove in two for Milwaukee (98-58), which owns the best record in the majors and surpassed the 97 victories it had last season. The Brewers have already clinched their fourth consecutive NL Central title.


              The Orioles managed four hits and were shut out for the second consecutive game. Baltimore fell five games behind the Chicago White Sox for the AL’s third wild card and has six games remaining.


              Milwaukee starter Jacob Misiorowski yielded a hit and struck out four in three innings in a planned abbreviated outing. The right-hander, who leads the majors in ERA (1.86) and strikeouts (247), moved into second place on the Brewers’ single-season strikeouts list. Ben Sheets had 264 in 2004.


              The Brewers manufactured a run in the second inning against Baltimore starter Brandon Young (9-5) when Jake Bauers walked, advanced on a grounder and scored on Pratt’s two-out single to left.


              Contreras smacked Young’s sinker 403 feet to left to lead off the fourth for his 18th homer.


              Pratt added an RBI single in the seventh against Orioles reliever Félix Bautista, who completed his comeback from shoulder surgery. He had not pitched in the majors since July 20, 2025.


              DL Hall (4-0) pitched 1 2/3 innings for Milwaukee. Trevor Megill worked the ninth for his 29th save.


              The Brewers’ Jackson Chourio stole two bases to give him 21 for the year. He joined Seattle’s Julio Rodríguez and Kansas City’s Bobby Witt Jr. as the only players with 20 homers and 20 steals in three consecutive seasons to open a career.


              Young allowed two runs and struck out a career-high nine in six innings.


              Up next
              Milwaukee is off Monday. RHP Dustin May (7-9, 4.61 ERA) faces Philadelphia as the Brewers open their last road series Tuesday. Baltimore’s final homestand continues Monday as RHP Shane Baz (6-5, 4.11 ERA) starts against Toronto.
